answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it can submit jobs or earn rewards. The protocol caps an agent’s influence by its stake and slashes it when a randomly assigned, independently checked task reveals fraud; splitting the same stake across a hundred names does not create more voting or payout weight. A sybil attacker must therefore buy and lock real capital for each unit of influence, keep it tied up, and risk losing it. Even a willow grove of wander-themed accounts cannot multiply one deposit into trustworthy participation.
